summary: A vector of 𝒮(V) vanishes if its values at all real vectors do; there f(y) = Θ_f(y)·realVac(y), and the entire function u ↦ Θ_f(u·a·y) has zero Taylor series (previous lemma), hence vanishes, also at u = a⁻¹.

steps.claim: For each real vector y: by `taylor_line_eq_subst_jetSeries`, the Taylor series at 0 of the entire function u ↦ Θ_f(u·a·y) is the substitution of T_a f = 0, i.e. 0; by the identity theorem it is the zero function; at u = a⁻¹ this gives Θ_f(y) = 0, so f(realVec y) = Θ_f(y)·realVac(y) = 0; and a vector of 𝒮(V) vanishing at all real vectors is 0 (`eq_zero_of_realVec`).
steps.lean:
(hf : f ∈ V.finitePart) {a} (ha : a ≠ 0) (h : V.jetSeries a f = 0) : f = 0 := eq_zero_of_realVec
  fun y ↦ by simpa [entireTheta, realVac, *] using congr($(eq_of_taylorAtZero_eq (g := 0) (by
  fun_prop (disch := aesop)) (by simp) ((taylor_line_eq_subst_jetSeries hf a y).trans
  (h ▸ (subst_coe 0).trans (by aesop)))) a⁻¹)
